title: Pooling problem: Alternate formulations and solution methods
contribution: Shows on refinery pooling instances that the choice among flow, proportion and hybrid bilinear formulations, and the availability of a good heuristic incumbent (alternating LP, VNS over LP vertices), largely decide how fast the authors' branch-and-cut QCQP algorithm solves the problem; reduces some literature instances to LPs or closed forms and solves larger instances exactly or approximately.
problem_entry: Industry-funded (Ultramar Canada) nonconvex bilinear problem; entry is 'how best to apply' the authors' own 2000 branch-and-cut QCQP code, motivated by the local-only guarantees of Haverly's recursion and SLP, the bound sensitivity of Al-Khayyal-Falk B&B and the need for heuristic incumbents (pp. 1-3, 15).
key_idea: Treat formulation as the main lever (proportion model has |W|-nP+|Y| nonlinear variables independent of attributes vs nA*nP+|Y| for flow; crossover nA=|W|/nP-1; hybrid for pools feeding pools) and build heuristics from the bilinear block structure: ALT alternates LPs over the two blocks, VNS shakes by k basis exchanges in one LP polyhedron and restarts ALT in the other (pp. 4-6, 11-12).
assumptions: Linear (volume-weighted) blending, more precise octane/distillation models excluded for complexity; pools with >=2 inflows and >=2 outflows; bounded feasible region and unique LP solutions for Prop. 4.1; absolute tolerance 1e-6 (pp. 3-4, 9, 11).
proof_devices: monotone-plus-bounded argument for alternating LPs, with the optimality notion (no improvement varying (x,y) or (x,z)) defined inside the proposition (Prop. 4.1, p. 11)
without-loss-of-generality flow rerouting to fix variables to zero and merge pools, reducing RT1 to an LP (pp. 7-8)
unit-cost decomposition (cost 30-10*alpha per unit of blend independent of feeds) giving an analytic optimum for F3-F5 (pp. 8-9)
symmetry-breaking constraint (larger pool carries at least the flow of the smaller) for RT2 (appendix, p. 15)
formulation-size accounting: bilinear variables per block, bilinear terms, L<=/Q<=/Q= counts and a crossover formula (pp. 6-7)
VNS neighborhood metric = symmetric difference of basic sets; |N_1(s)| <= 2n1+n2+n3, equality when nondegenerate (p. 12)
experiments: Exact: 12 literature instances + GP1 on a Sun Ultra-60, each run cold and warm (optimum + objective cut) to price the optimality proof, failures shown (memory limit, AST4 proof slower, objective cut hurting outer approximation); cross-study CPU table with raw and CPU-speed-adjusted ratios conceding easy instances to Adhya et al.; heuristics MSLP vs MALT vs VNS with % error vs exact, per-instance parameters, feasible-start rate (0/10,000 -> ~25% on RT2), and 19 random instances (nA up to 30); no seeds/replications or profiles reported (pp. 9-15).
positioning: Two-page review sorted by guarantee (local: Haverly recursion, SLP/distributive recursion, Benders; epsilon-global: GOP, Al-Khayyal-Falk; proportion/duality: Ben-Tal et al.; latest: Adhya et al. with BARON); factual, mechanism-based critique; industrial lineage (Shell, Exxon, Texaco) cited; self-citation for reformulation as a research tool (pp. 2-4).
writing: Core claim in the introduction's second paragraph before notation; roadmap previews results; systematic hedging (suggest/appears/seems); bounded novelty claim for ALT ('to our best knowledge' first computational experience); one proposition vs many tables with a worked count to decode Table 1; no conclusion, ends with observation bullets (pp. 1, 3, 6, 9-11, 15).
limits_future: Limits stated concretely: memory limit of the current exact implementation, degeneracy defeating VNS shaking on AST, open theory for the solution-dependent extreme-point discretization, linear blending only, hard feasibility of starting points; no future-work section (pp. 4, 9, 12, 15).

method_links.note: Heuristics (MALT, VNS) propose incumbents and branch-and-cut certifies global optimality; the certifier is B&C rather than a Poll; the cold/warm protocol prices the proposer and AST4 shows a good incumbent can slow the certifier; this VNS precedes the VNS Search in MADS (JOGO 2008).
Model-before-algorithm applied to variable choice (flow/proportion/hybrid) and pool elimination rather than constraint classification.
Weak guarantee stated precisely (block-wise local optimum under unique LP solutions) and the missing VNS theory admitted; no counterexamples or necessity tests.
Industry-funded problem; all instance data online at www.gerad.ca/Charles.Audet; privately communicated RT2 printed in the appendix; random-instance family with size ranges.
Concedes easy instances to the state-of-the-art competitor, adjusts cross-machine times by CPU speed, reports failures, tests against the industrial default SLP.
Currency is CPU time, heuristic parameters set per instance, no profiles, no replications or seeds reported; AST4 omitted from the text's speed-up claim though present in Table 5.
Own C++ branch-and-cut code (2000) reused as the instrument; its memory limits reported as limits of the current implementation; no long-lived product.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Counts bilinear variables, terms and constraints per formulation, derives the crossover nA=|W|/nP-1, then checks against solve times and notes where counts mislead (BT5).
Shows RT1 reduces to an LP and F3-F5 have analytic solutions before benchmarking on them.
Runs the exact method cold and warm (optimum + objective cut) to measure what a heuristic incumbent buys; reports cases where it hurts.

transferable: Before benchmarking on inherited instances, apply rerouting/dominance arguments to fix variables and merge nodes, and publish which instances collapse to an LP or closed form (pp. 7-9).

Compare formulations with a size table (linear vars; bilinear vars per block; bilinear terms; L<=/Q<=/Q=), give the crossover formula, then validate by solving and report where counts mislead (pp. 6-7, 9).
Price a heuristic by running the exact method cold and warm (optimum + objective cut); explain the cases where warm is slower (pp. 9-10).

For bilinear problems: local search = alternating LP solves over the two blocks; shaking = random extreme point k basis exchanges away, alternating subspaces; distance = symmetric difference of basic sets (pp. 11-12).
Report the feasible-start rate and the tricks that raised it (sparse random starts with P(zero)=0.5, random choice of which block to fix) (pp. 12, 15).
In cross-paper timing tables give raw and CPU-speed-adjusted ratios and concede the instances the competitor wins (p. 10).
When a heuristic seeds another method, include its time in that method's reported time (p. 13).
Define the weak optimality notion inside the proposition statement so the guarantee cannot be over-read (p. 11).
coauthors: J. Brimberg, P. Hansen, S. Le Digabel, N. Mladenović

quotes.text: The results clearly show that the type of model formulation chosen and initial heuristic used may significantly affect the performance of the exact method.
This seems to justify the joint use of a heuristic to obtain a good incumbent solution.
